"''Well, the trainer's prepped. Been using it a lot lately with the newer recruits.|Ezra Bridger and a Rebel soldier|}} The '''RZ-1T''', also known as '''RZ-1T A-wing''',''[[Rebel Starfighters Owners' Workshop Manual]]'' was a model of [[RZ-1 A-wing interceptor|A-wing]] [[Trainer (starship)|trainer]] [[starship]] used by the early rebellion against the [[Galactic Empire]] and later the [[Alliance to Restore the Republic|Rebel Alliance]], to train aspiring rebel [[pilot]]s. The starship, developed in the early days of the rebellion, bore many similarities to the base RZ-1,{{Film|VI}} such as a wedge-shaped hull, dual [[laser cannon]]s and [[sublight engine]]s, and an internal [[hyperdrive]]. Due to its role as a pilot training vehicle, the RZ-1T also featured an additional seat reserved for an instructor in the back of the [[cockpit]]. One RZ-1T was stationed at [[Phoenix Cell]]'s [[Chopper Base|secret base]] in [[2 BBY]]According to ''[[Star Wars: Absolutely Everything You Need to Know, Updated and Expanded]]'', [[Maul]]'s final confrontation with [[Obi-Wan Kenobi]] in the ''[[Star Wars Rebels]]'' episode "[[Twin Suns (episode)|Twin Suns]]" took place thirty [[Standard year|years]] after Kenobi first [[Duel on Tatooine|saw]] him on [[Tatooine]]. Since ''[[Star Wars: Galactic Atlas]]'' dates that event to [[32 BBY]], "Twin Suns" is set in [[2 BBY]]. and used to train the rebel cell's new recruits. During this time, [[Padawan]] [[Ezra Bridger]] and [[Jedi Knight]] [[Kanan Jarrus]] used the RZ-1T to travel to [[Vizsla Keep 09]] and rescue their [[Spectres|friends]] from the former [[Sith]] [[Sith Lord|Lord]], [[Maul]]. Some time later, Bridger took the trainer without authorization to the [[desert]] [[planet]] of [[Tatooine]] in order to meet with [[Jedi Master]] [[Obi-Wan Kenobi]] and warn him of Maul. However, after landing, Bridger and [[C1-10P]], who had stowed away aboard the vessel, were ambushed by the native [[Tusken Raider]]s. After taking six bolts from the Raiders' [[blaster rifle]]s, the RZ-1T exploded. In [[0 ABY]], a dilapidated RZ-1T was in the possession of the [[Dreamers]], an [[Terrorist|extremist]] rebel group formed from the remnants of [[Saw Gerrera]]'s [[Partisans]]. The trainer was kept in a cache of stolen ships in the cell's [[Dreamers' encampment|encampment]] on the planet [[Jeosyn]]. During a [[Dreamers Infiltration|mission]] conducted by the Empire's [[Inferno Squad]] to infiltrate and integrate within the rebel cell, [[Agent]] [[Gideon Hask]] often went flying in the RZ-1T with the group's leader, [[Staven]]. ==Behind the scenes== [[File:KyboRenEscapes-TRoKR.png|thumb|Earliest appearance of a "two seater" A-Wing]] The RZ-1T was a model of starship that first appeared, albeit identified only as a "trainer," in "[[The Holocrons of Fate]]," the second episode of the [[Star Wars Rebels Season Three|third season]] of the [[canon]] animated series ''[[Star Wars Rebels]]'', released on [[October 1]], [[2016]].{{RebelsRecon|xtgm8dAq2bU|#3.01: Inside "Steps Into Shadow" | Star Wars Rebels|sw_url=video/rebels-recon-inside-steps-into-shadow}} It was later identified as an RZ-1T in the starship's [[Databank (2014-)|Databank]] entry on [[StarWars.com]]. The very first appearance of a two-seater A-Wing was in the [[Star Wars Legends|''Star Wars'' Legends]] animated series ''[[Star Wars: Droids: The Adventures of R2-D2 and C-3PO]]'', in the episode "[[The Revenge of Kybo Ren]]."{{DroidsCite|The Revenge of Kybo Ren}} Though [[The New Essential Guide to Characters|later Legends materials]] retconed the ship as a version of the [[R-22 Spearhead starfighter]], production materials from the show at the time labelled it simply as a "Two Seater A-Wing."''[[The New Essential Guide to Characters]]'' ==Appearances== {{Mediacat|imagecat=Images of
